\section{Gaussian Space --- Indicator Regularity}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.IndicatorRegularity
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Indicator Regularity: Introduction}
At nonzero noise scale, averaged indicators have a product Gaussian density representation. Differentiation of this density gives global bounds and Lipschitz regularity for their ordinary derivatives.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Indicator Regularity: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Density formula for the averaged indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_eq_integral_density}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_affine_gaussian_pi_eq_density}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, let $u\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$\sin u\ne0$, and let $x\in\mathbb R^n$. Then
\[
u_u(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\left(\prod_{i=1}^n p_{\sin^2 u}(\cos
u\,x_i,z_i)\right)1_A(z)\,dz,
\]
where $u_u(x)=\int 1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin u\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$ and $p_v(c,z)$ is the density
at $z$ of a Gaussian random variable with mean $c$ and variance $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Norm bound for cosine scaling]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_cosineScaling_le_one}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$ and every $u\in\mathbb R$, the linear map on $\mathbb R^n$
given by $x\mapsto(\cos u)x$ has operator norm at most $1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of an averaged Gaussian indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_averagedGaussianIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator_eq_integral_density, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_integral_gaussianProductDensity}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $u\in\mathbb R$
satisfy $\sin u\ne0$. For $x\in\mathbb R^n$, define $F(x)=\int 1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin
u\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure. The function $F$ is
differentiable at every $x$, and its derivative is the linear functional obtained by
composing multiplication by $\cos u$ with the integral, over $z\in\mathbb R^n$ with
respect to Lebesgue measure, of $1_A(z)$ times the derivative in the mean vector $c$ of
the product Gaussian density $\prod_{i=1}^n p_{\sin^2u}(c_i,z_i)$, evaluated at $c=\cos
u\,x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative bound for a Gaussian indicator average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_fderiv_averagedGaussianIndicator_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_cosineScaling_le_one, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_integral_gaussianProductDensityDerivative_smul_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let
$u\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\sin u\ne0$. For every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, the derivative at $x$
of the Gaussian conditional indicator average with angle $u$ has norm at most
\[
n\left(1+\frac{1}{\sin^2 u}\right).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lipschitz continuity under linear contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzWith_comp_contraction}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $E$ be a real normed vector space, let $D:E\to\mathcal L(E,\mathbb R)$ be Lipschitz
with constant $C\ge0$, and let $L:E\to E$ be continuous linear with operator norm at
most $1$. Then the map $x\mapsto D(Lx)\circ L$ is Lipschitz with constant $C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lipschitz derivative of a Gaussian indicator average]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzWith_fderiv_averagedGaussianIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasFDerivAt_averagedGaussianIndicator, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzWith_comp_contraction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lipschitzWith_integral_gaussianProductDensityDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.norm_cosineScaling_le_one}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $u\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$\sin u\ne0$. Define $v_u(x)=\int 1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin u\,Y)\,d\gamma_n(Y)$ for standard
Gaussian $Y$. The derivative map $x\mapsto Dv_u(x)$ is Lipschitz with constant
$2n^2/\sin^2u$, using the maximum norm on $\mathbb R^n$ and the operator norm on linear
functionals.
\end{lemma}
